name: Peanut Tofu-Cauliflower Bake with Bell Pepper, Edamame & Rice

instructions.primary_message: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Meanwhile, using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ cups jasmine rice
3 cup water

instructions.primary_message: Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, place oil and spices in a large bowl; stir to combine the spice paste.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp toasted sesame oil
¾ tsp garlic powder
¾ tsp turmeric, ground
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Medium dice tofu. Add to the bowl with the spice paste, along with the cauliflower, and gently stir to coat. Divide between two baking sheets and spread out in a single layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheets in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until tofu and cauliflower are golden brown, 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, trim, and seed bell peppers; small dice. Place in the reserved bowl.
Place edamame in the colander and rinse under hot, running water (from the tap) to defrost; add to the bowl with the bell pepper. Set aside.
When the tofu and cauliflower are done, remove from the oven. Add to the bowl, along with the peanut sauce, and stir to combine.
To serve, divide rice between plates or bowls; top with tofu and veggies. Enjoy!
